newFindings.title: Amendment 33 claims every refusal carries a mayHaveRun flag; most do not
newFindings.evidence: ADR-0115 amendment 33: 'Every refusal carries error.code and a mayHaveRun flag.' At 19e5427a, hubCall.ts refusals with no data/mayHaveRun include invalid-arguments (272, 312), hub-unavailable (288), unknown-callee (307), product-not-connected (325, 356), product-credential-unavailable (340), binding-revoked (348, 453) and idempotency-conflict (468); access-required (shared/access.ts accessRefusal) carries data.request, not mayHaveRun. Only cancelled, idempotency-capacity, outcome-unknown, answer-not-kept and the not-sent forward codes carry it. An agent reading the contract could treat an absent flag as unknown.
newFindings.fix: Either add {mayHaveRun:false} to every pre-forward refusal (and test it), or restate: 'the flag is present when the call reached or may have reached the forwarder; its absence means nothing was sent'. Add product-refused/product-unreachable rows (D-8).

newFindings.title: The CHANGELOG 0.3.1 lead paragraph is process text that the new finalization check does not catch
newFindings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md 0.3.1 lead: 'The release pull request renames this heading to `## 0.3.1` and finalizes the notes; the version bump and the tag follow the third verification iteration …'. release-mac.mjs changelogProblem refuses only an '(unreleased)' heading or 'not released yet|(unreleased)' in the body. If the heading alone is renamed, this paragraph passes preflight and is published as the release notes.
newFindings.fix: Remove the lead paragraph in the release PR (or now, replacing it with a user-facing summary), or add a test-backed check for a release-process marker.
